facts.fact: The French Treasury note says Djibouti has no specific AI policy or regulatory framework yet.

DJI.note: No government body's use of AI is stated; the road-monitoring project is a company's with a ports corridor firm.
Only road monitoring by a company partnership is named, with no public sector system stated.

facts.fact: The French Treasury note says Vision 2035 has no AI roadmap and the 2023 Djibouti Smart Nation roadmap does not mention AI, so Djibouti has no AI policy yet.

DJI.note: No AI model, dataset or AI computing is stated as built or hosted in the country.
Nothing stated on digital-skills training for civil servants.

facts.fact: The French Treasury note says the Djibouti Data Centre, built in 2013 by Wingu, is a neutral data centre next to the cable landing station.
The French Treasury note says Wingu inaugurated a new Tier 3 data centre at the TO7 technology park in November 2024.

DJI.note: Only a private coding school founded in 2024 is named, not a national programme.

facts.fact: The French Treasury note says the data centre operator also runs the Djibouti Internet Exchange (DjIX), a neutral and independent exchange point.
The French Treasury note says nine submarine cables are connected to Djibouti's coast, with three more expected in 2025 and one in 2026.

DJI.note: The state information systems agency is named only as holding a conference; no staff running systems is stated.

facts.fact: The French Treasury note says the Djibouti Data Centre was built by the French company Wingu.

DJI.note: Only a university conference and hackathon on AI are named, no research on digital policy.
Nothing stated on consultation of people outside government.
No school internet figure or compulsory curriculum is stated.
No startup law, label or fund is stated.

facts.fact: The French Treasury note says the Centre de Leadership et d'Entreprenariat has an incubator seeking to host startups with AI-related projects.
